description: An illustration of a micrometer, vernier callipers, a measuring tape and two dial timers.
Photograph of the International Prototype kilogram inside a glass enclosure; caption: “The International Prototype kilogram”
A measuring tape labelled “STANLEY POWERLOCK 25”.
A metre rule marked 0, 1, 2 and 3, with viewing points A, B and C. The labels show “1.5 cm incorrect” at A, “1.8 cm correct” at B and “2.0 cm incorrect” at C.
Vernier callipers labelled Inside jaws (C, D), Outside jaws (A, B), Vernier scale, Main scale and Tail; the instrument and its scales are shown with measurement markings.
Main scale marked 4 and 5, with a Vernier scale marked 0, 5 and 10; labels Main scale and Vernier scale.
Two Vernier-scale diagrams, (a) and (b), each beside a Main scale marked 0, 1 and 2; the Vernier scales show 0 and 10, with the zero positions differing between the diagrams.

Micrometer screw gauge labelled “anvil”, “spindle”, “sleeve” and “ratchet”. Text: “The object that is to be measured is placed between the anvil and the spindle.” “The thimble is turned to move the spindle.” “The ratchet prevents over tightening by making a click sound when the micrometer is ready to be read.” Marking on the frame: “0-25×0.01mm”.

Three screw-gauge scale illustrations labelled (a), (b) and (c), showing a horizontal reference line and circular scale markings. Each has a “0” on the main scale. Circular scale markings shown: (a) 15, 10, 5, 0, 95, 90, 85; (b) 20, 15, 10, 5, 0, 95, 90; (c) 10, 5, 0, 95, 90, 85, 80.
Screw-gauge scale showing sleeve markings 0 and 5 and circular scale markings 30, 25 and 20.
Two spring balances, one with a narrow graduated scale and one with a circular dial, both with hooks.
A physical balance with two pans suspended from a beam.
Mechanical stopwatch held in a hand. Caption: Mechanical Stopwatch.
Digital stopwatch with digital display. Caption: Digital Stopwatch.
Hourglass with sand in the upper and lower chambers. Caption: Sandclock.
Measuring cylinder with scale labels 10, 20, 30 and 40; arrows indicate “wrong”, “correct” and “wrong” eye positions for reading the meniscus. Caption: Measuring cylinder.
Two graduated cylinders; the initial liquid level in the left cylinder is labelled A, and the higher liquid level in the right cylinder, with a solid immersed in it, is labelled B.

Two diagrams (a) and (b) showing a displacement can with a side opening and a beaker; in (b), a body is immersed in the can and overflowing water is collected in the beaker. Labels: Side opening, Beaker, Body. Caption: Fig. 1.13 Displacement can or Overflow can
A metallic ball placed between two wooden blocks beside a ruler marked 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5.
A black rod placed above a ruler, with ruler markings and labels 0cm, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7.

Three circular targets labeled (a), (b), and (c). In (a), three arrow marks are clustered together away from the bullseye; caption: “Precise not accurate”. In (b), three arrow marks are spread apart around the target; caption: “Accurate not precise”. In (c), arrow marks are clustered at the bullseye; caption: “Accurate and precise”.
An electronic timer.
Vernier callipers scale labelled “Main scale” and “Vernier scale”; main scale is marked 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, and Vernier scale is marked 0, 5, 10.
A ruler and an object, with three viewing positions marked A, B, and C and readings 5.9 cm, 6.0 cm, and 6.1 cm, respectively.
Micrometer screw gauge showing a main scale marked 0 and a circular scale marked 60, 70 and 80.
Race cars driving on a racetrack, with spectators in grandstands.
Compass axes labelled N, S, W, E and O, with vector v pointing northeast and angle θ from east toward north; caption: A vector v making an angle θ towards north from east.
Cartesian axes labelled y, y′, x′, x and O, with vector F pointing up and to the right at 30° to the x-axis; caption: A vector F making angle 30° with x-axis.
Horizontal x-axis labeled x′ on the left and x on the right, vertical y-axis labeled y above and y′ below, with origin O. Vector F points from O toward Q at 60° above the positive x-axis.

Horizontal x-axis labeled x′ on the left and x on the right, vertical y-axis labeled y above and y′ below, with origin O. Two arrows point up and right from O: the shorter vector is labeled 3cm and makes a 30° angle with the positive x-axis; the longer vector is labeled 4cm and makes a 60° angle with the positive x-axis.

Vector diagram with axes x, y, x′ and y′ meeting at O. Vector v is the resultant, labelled 6.8 cm and at 49° to the x-axis; vector v_1 is labelled 3 cm and at 30° to the x-axis; vector v_2 is labelled 4 cm and at 60° to the dashed horizontal line.
A man seated on a stationary motorcycle.
A man riding a motorcycle.
A train; caption: The motion of a train is translatory motion.
(a) An irregular path with arrows; caption: Irregular path. (b) A bee; caption: The motion of bee is random motion.
A Ferris wheel; caption: Circular Motion.
An electric fan; caption: Rotatory motion of a fan.
A child on a swing; caption: Vibratory motion.
A car follows a curved path from A to B. A straight arrow from A to B is labelled d, with its arrowhead at B.
A car travelling on a circular road.
A cheetah running on land and a sailfish leaping out of the water.
Photograph of a volcanic eruption. Caption: Mount st. Helens erupted in 1980, causing rocks to travel at velocities up to 400 km h⁻¹.
A time-lapse photo of motorway traffic at night, with light trails from vehicles.
Two cars travelling on a road, with a blue car overtaking a red car.
A hand dropping a red apple, with a vertical series of red apple images below it; the spaces between the images widen downward.
Two views of a plane on a runway. The first is labeled v_i = 0 and t = 0; the second has a rightward arrow labeled v_f and is labeled t = 20 s.

A graph-paper grid with perpendicular horizontal and vertical axes intersecting at O; x′ is marked at the left end of the horizontal axis, x at the right end, y above the vertical axis, and y′ below it.
A straight-line graph with t (min) along the x-axis, marked 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and S (km) along the y-axis, marked 1.2, 2.4, 3.6, 4.8, 6.0; plotted points lie on the line.

An upward-curving graph with t (min) along the x-axis, marked 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and S (km) along the y-axis, marked 0, 1.000, 2.000, 3.000, 4.000, 5.000, 6.000; dashed guides indicate the curve’s values at t = 2, 3, 4, 5.

A curved distance–time graph, increasing and flattening from (0, 2.0) to (5, 5.0). The vertical axis is labelled S (km), with values 0, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0 and 5.0; the horizontal axis is labelled t (min), with values 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5. Dashed guide lines mark the plotted values.

A horizontal graph at S = 1.2, with vertical lines down to the horizontal axis at t = 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5. The vertical axis is labelled S (km), with values 0.4, 0.8, 1.2, 1.6 and 2.0, and is marked y; the horizontal axis is labelled t (min) and is marked x. The origin is marked 0.

Distance-time graph with a straight rising line from O through P and Q; horizontal axis labelled t (s) and x, vertical axis labelled S (m) and y; points O, P, Q and R; dashed lines marking t_1, t_2, S_1 and S_2; segments labelled (t_2 − t_1) and (S_2 − S_1); angle θ at P.

Graph with a straight line rising from origin O. Vertical axis Y is labelled v (m s⁻¹) and marked 8, 16, 24, 32, 40; horizontal axis X is labelled t (s) and marked 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Dashed lines indicate values (1, 8), (2, 16), (3, 24), (4, 32), and (5, 40).

Graph with a horizontal line at speed 20 and open circles at times 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5. Vertical axis y is labelled v (m s⁻¹) and marked 10, 20, 30; horizontal axis x is labelled t (s) and marked 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, with origin O.

A speed-time graph with vertical Y-axis and horizontal X-axis, origin O, and a rising straight line passing through P and Q. Horizontal dashed lines mark v_1 and v_2; vertical dashed lines mark t_1 and t_2, with R at the intersection of the v_1 level and the t_2 line. The graph labels include v, (v_2 − v_1), (t_2 − t_1), and t (s).

A speed-time graph with vertical Y-axis labelled v (m s⁻¹), values 10, 20, and 30, and horizontal X-axis labelled t (s), with ticks 1 to 5. A horizontal line at 20 has open circles at 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5. The graph also labels v_1, v_2, t_1, and t_2.
A shaded rectangle on a speed-time graph, with vertical axis Y marked v, horizontal axis X marked t, origin O, and rectangle dimensions v and t.

A speed-time graph with vertical axis Y marked v, horizontal axis X marked t, origin O, and a shaded right-angled triangle OAB beneath a rising line from O to A; A is at speed v and time t, and B is at time t on the horizontal axis.

A distance-time graph with vertical axis marked distance and horizontal axis marked time. Three lines are labelled cyclist A, cyclist B and cyclist C; cyclist A rises steeply, cyclist B rises and then becomes horizontal, and cyclist C rises with a gentler slope.
Four pairs of objects are shown side by side: a light, round object and a heavier, flat object.
Vertical streaks appear above a small rock and a larger rock.

A displacement–time graph with vertical axis S and horizontal axis t. A straight line from the origin rises to the upper right and is labelled A; a horizontal line above the origin is labelled B. The lines cross.

Four v–t graphs, each with vertical axis v and horizontal axis t: (a) a rising curve that starts above the origin and bends upward; (b) a straight rising line from the origin; (c) a straight rising line that starts above the origin; (d) a straight falling line that starts above the origin and reaches the horizontal axis.

Four velocity v–time t graphs labelled (a), (b), (c) and (d). In (a), v decreases linearly from v at 0 to 0 at T/2, then increases to v at T. In (b), lines from positive v and negative v meet at 0 at T/2. In (c), v decreases linearly from positive v through 0 at T/2 to negative v at T. In (d), v increases from 0 to v at T/2, then decreases to 0 at T. The axes are labelled v and t; the graphs show 0, T/2 and T.

Distance - time graph with vertical axis labelled “Distance → S (km)” and horizontal axis labelled “Time → t (min)”. The vertical scale is 0 to 2.0 in increments of 0.2; the horizontal scale is 0 to 20 in increments of 2. Segment a rises from (0, 0) to (6, 2.0), segment b is horizontal from (6, 2.0) to (10, 2.0), and segment c falls from (10, 2.0) to (20, 0).
A man pushing a loaded wheelbarrow at a construction site.
A tree bearing apples, with one apple falling beside the trunk
Two balloons with plus signs are held by a hand; arrows point outward from each balloon, both labelled “Force”.
A horseshoe magnet with its poles labelled N and S, with pins attracted near the S pole.
A hand moves a magnet near a coil connected by wires to a meter. Caption: A moving magnet produces electric current

A nucleus made of red and orange particles, with blue particles on light-blue orbital paths around it and four red arrows pointing inward toward the nucleus. Caption: “The binding force of protons and neutrons in the nucleus”.
A cluster of protons and neutrons, labelled “Proton” and “Neutron”, with an “Electron” labelled above the cluster and an arrow pointing right to “Neutrino”.
A book on a table with an arrow labelled “Applied force” pointing to the right.

A square with arrows pointing upward, downward, left and right. The upward arrow is labelled “Normal force,” the downward arrow “Weight,” the left arrow “Friction” and the right arrow “Applied force.”
A green and white book rests on a round wooden table.

“A Demonstration of Property of Inertia”; two images show a table cloth being pulled abruptly from beneath objects on a table. Caption: “When the table cloth is pulled abruptly, the objects remain in their original position on the table.”

A hand presses down on a spring standing on a flat platform. A red arrow points downward onto the hand and a red arrow points upward from below the platform. The labels A and B appear beside the spring.
An astronaut throws a wrench. The wrench has a left-pointing arrow labelled F, and the astronaut has a right-pointing arrow labelled R.
A block resting on a table, with upward arrows labelled F_n and downward arrows labelled w.
A gun pointing to the right, with a leftward arrow labelled R and a rightward arrow labelled F.
A rocket launching, with exhaust and smoke billowing downward.
A person running, shown mid-stride.
A swimmer moving through a swimming pool.
A mechanical balance with a flat pan on one side and a bowl-shaped pan on the other.
A mechanical platform balance with a large platform, upright beam, and a small hanging weight.
An electronic balance with a metal bowl on top, a display, and keypad.
A pocket balance with a circular ring at the top and a hook at the bottom; the scale is marked in increments from 0 to 20.
A digital force meter with a hook at the top, a display reading 1.68, buttons labelled UNIT, PEAK and ZERO, and a lower display reading 89.
A hand holds a spring balance above a blue shape; the text reads “The weight of 100 g mass is 1 N.”
Two hands rubbing together, with two red arrows pointing in opposite directions.
A tyre showing its tread pattern.
A block on a horizontal table is connected by a string over a pulley to a hanging pan. Arrows on the block are labelled F_n upwards, mg downwards, F_s to the left and F = T to the right.
A paratrooper descends beneath an open parachute.
Knee joint, with labels Bones and Lubricating Fluid.
A car wheel with a flat portion in contact with the ground.
A hovercraft moving over water.
Ball bearings; caption: Fig. 3.24
A car with streamline air-flow lines passing over it; caption: Streamline air flow over a speedy car
A cricketer drawing his hands back as a ball approaches.
An arrow penetrating an apple; another arrow indicates the opposing force.
An open cardboard box containing glassware wrapped in protective packing material.
A car colliding with a barrier, with the front crumple zone compressed; the car interior shows passengers, airbags and seatbelts. Labels: Crumple zone, Air bag, Seatbelts.

Two balls labelled m_1 and m_2 move in the same direction, with arrows labelled v_1 and v_2. During collision, opposing arrows are labelled F and −F. After collision, the balls are labelled m_1 and m_2, with arrows in the same direction labelled v′_1 and v′_2.

Two identical balls shown before, during and after a collision. Before collision, the blue ball moves right with v₁ and the pink ball is at rest, v₂ = 0. During collision, the balls exert forces F and −F. After collision, the blue ball is at rest, v′₁ = 0, and the pink ball moves right with v′₂ = v₁.
A rigid body with three forces at different points: F_1 and F_2 point upwards, and F_3 points downwards.
Coordinate axes x and x′ horizontally, y and y′ vertically, with origin O; vectors F_1, F_2 and F_3 extend from O at angles 30°, 45° and 60° to the x-axis, respectively.

Coordinate axes x and x′ horizontally, y and y′ vertically, with origin O; head-to-tail vectors F_1 (2.0 cm, 30°), F_2 (3.0 cm, 45°) and F_3 (2.5 cm, 60°); resultant F (7.1 cm) is at 43° to the x-axis.
An oval rigid body with points A and B, shown rotating about the z-axis through O; x-, y- and z-axes are shown. Labels: Axis of rotation, Rigid body, A, B, x, y, z, O, Fig. 4.3.
A see-saw with a lighter child on the left and a heavier child on the right, with a central pivot and arrows showing moment arms on both sides. Labels: Pivot, Moment arm, Moment arm.
A door with a handle.
A spanner holding a nut; upward force F is applied at point A, and upward force F′ at point B. Labels: Nut, A, B.
An object with axis O and point P; force F acts vertically upward at P, perpendicular to OP. Labels: O, axis, ℓ = r, P, F.
An object with axis O and horizontal line ℓ to point P; force F acts upwards at an angle θ to the horizontal, with vertical component F sinθ. Labels: O, ℓ, P, θ, F sinθ, F.
An object with axis O and horizontal line ℓ to point P; force F acts at an angle θ to the horizontal. The perpendicular moment arm is marked ℓ sinθ = r. Labels: O, ℓ, P, θ, α, ℓ sinθ = r, F.

A green body with point A on the left and point B on the right, with point O between them. A downward arrow labelled F₁ acts at A, and an upward arrow labelled F₂ acts at B. The distances from A to O and O to B are labelled r₁ and r₂.
A person’s hands holding a vehicle steering wheel.
A horizontal spanner with a nut at the left end and a circular end at the right. An upward arrow labelled F is shown at the right end, with a dotted horizontal line extending from it.

“Beam of light” above a diagram of perpendicular x- and y-axes, with the origin O, points A, B and C, vector F from O to C at angle θ to the x-axis, green horizontal component F_x from O to A, magenta vertical component F_y from O to B, and dashed lines from B to C and C to A. The beam has downward arrows. The axes are labelled x and y.

Diagram of perpendicular x- and y-axes, with the origin O, points A, B and C, vector F from O to C at angle θ to the x-axis, green horizontal component F_x from O to A, magenta vertical component F_y from A to C, and dashed lines from B to C and C to A. The axes are labelled x and y.
A tight rope walker standing on a rope and holding a bamboo stick, with water and a shoreline in the background.
Right-angled triangle ABC with angle θ at A and a right angle at B. AB is labelled Base, BC is labelled Perpendicular and AC is labelled Hypotenuse.

A vector F angled upward to the right from O, making an angle of 60° with the horizontal x-axis. Its horizontal component is labelled F cos θ, its vertical component is labelled F sin θ; the axes are labelled x and y.

A horizontal metre rule supported at CG on a wedge, with weights w_1 and w_2 hanging to the left and weight w_3 hanging to the right. The distances are labelled l_1 from w_1 to CG, l_2 from w_2 to CG and l_3 from CG to w_3.

A horizontal metre stick is pinned at O on the left. The distance d is marked from O to the point where a 60 N force acts at 30° to the stick; a 18 N force acts downward at the free end, marked 1.0 m from O.
An irregular object with multiple downward arrows showing gravitational forces acting on various particles. Caption: “Gravitational force acting on various particles”.
An irregular object marked C with a single downward arrow showing the resultant gravitational force. Caption: “Resultant gravitational force”.

Irregular shaped plane lamina shown suspended from points of suspension; dashed vertical and diagonal lines intersect at CG in Fig. 4.15(b). Labels: “Points of suspension”, “CG”, “Fig. 4.15(a)”, “Fig. 4.15(b)”, “Irregular shaped plane lamina”.
A bowl labelled “CG”. Caption: “Centre of gravity of a bowl is outside the material.”
A rotating wrench in successive positions sliding along a frictionless floor, with yellow dots marking its centre of mass.
A group of people balancing in a pose. Caption: “This is a fascinating scene of equilibrium.”
A book rests on a table. An upward arrow labeled F_n and a downward arrow labeled w act on the book.
A horizontal beam is attached to a wall, supported by a sloping rope, and has a weight hanging from its end. Labels: Wall, Rope, Beam, Weight.
A paratrooper descends beneath an open parachute.
A group of paratroopers in freefall.

Two cases showing forces acting on a rigid body. In (a), F_2 points left and F_1 points right along the same horizontal line through points A, O and B. In (b), F_2 points left at point B and F_1 points right at point A, with O between them and a vertical dotted line connecting A and B. Labels (a) and (b).
A balancing toy with two weights hanging from the ends of an arched support, mounted on a stand.

A picture suspended by two vertical strings from a horizontal support. The left string has an upward arrow labeled T_1 and is attached at A; the right string has an upward arrow labeled T_2 and is attached at B. O is midway between A and B, with 20 cm from A to O and 20 cm from O to B. A downward arrow labeled w acts at the centre of the picture.

Two cone diagrams on a horizontal baseline: (a) an upright cone with an upward F_n arrow and a downward w arrow through G; (b) a tilted cone with an upward F_n arrow at the base, a downward w arrow through G, and dashed construction lines. Labels (a), (b), F_n, w, and G.
Two diagrams of a cone, (a) upright on its tip and (b) tilted. Labels shown are (a), (b), G, w, O and F_r.
A cylinder resting on a horizontal surface, with an upward arrow F_r and a downward arrow w through G.
A ball and a cone resting on their surfaces.
A double decker bus tilting.
Two illustrations of a seated person on a chair, labeled (a) and (b). In (a), the chair is upright; in (b), it is tilted back on its legs. Both show G and w; (b) also shows an upward F_n arrow.
Three balancing toys: (a) a metal cylinder with curved arms and weights, (b) a balancing airplane toy on a stand, and (c) a bird-shaped toy on a stand.
A wooden balancing-toy setup with a plank, colorful stacking rings and peg figures, with loose rings and a small figure beside it.
A red racing car on a track.
A circle with arrows tangent to its circumference and arrows directed toward its centre; an upward arrow at the right is labelled v, and an inward arrow is labelled F.
A person whirling a stone attached to a string in a circular path, shown as a dashed ellipse with arrows indicating motion.
A circular path with O at the centre and P on the circumference; a radius from O to P is labelled T, and a tangent from P toward Q is labelled v.
The Earth with a satellite and a dashed red circular orbit around it.
A washing machine drum with a central agitator.
A cream separator with a bowl on top and a glass beside it.
Three illustrations labelled (a), (b), and (c): (a) a cone resting on its circular base; (b) a ball on top of a dome; (c) a cylinder lying horizontally on its side.
A door with hinges along its left edge, a knob on the right edge, a dashed line from the hinge to the knob labelled 1.2 m, and a force arrow labelled F.
A metre rule balanced on a support labelled C.G, with a weight w hanging 40 cm to the left and a 4 N weight hanging 30 cm to the right.

A box rests at the left end of a crowbar angled upward to the right. The bar is supported near the box; the distances shown are 5 cm from the box to the support and 30 cm from the support to the downward force F at the right end.
A horizontal spanner with its head at the left and a nut at the right; a vertical force F is applied at the right end, with a horizontal dashed line extending to the right.

A ball hangs from a slanting rope attached to a horizontal ceiling. The angle between the rope and ceiling is 60°. The rope is labelled T, and a horizontal arrow pointing right toward the ball is labelled F.

A signboard is suspended by two vertical wires labelled T_1 and T_2. The distances from the centre to the wires are marked 2 m on each side. The board is labelled “Signboard”, with a downward arrow labelled 200 N.

A joint is connected to a horizontal string at the right and a slanting string to a horizontal support above. The angle between the slanting string and the horizontal support is 60°. A block hangs below the joint and is labelled 150 N.
A wide waterfall flowing over a cliff, with trees and river visible.
A girl studying at a desk with books beside her.
A man standing with a load of bricks on his head.
Two blue blocks shown at different positions on a horizontal surface, each with a right-pointing arrow labeled F; the distance between the positions is marked S.
A man wearing a yellow helmet pushing against a wall.
Two blocks moving horizontally to the right, each with a force F acting at angle θ to the direction of motion; the component F cos θ acts horizontally, and the distance between the blocks is S.
A person carrying a bag; an upward arrow is labelled Force F, and a diagonal arrow pointing to the right is labelled Displacement S.

A force-distance graph with vertical axis Force and horizontal axis Distance. The vertical axis is marked O and P, the horizontal axis O and R, and the shaded rectangular area OPQR is labelled “Shaded area work done”; F marks the vertical height and S marks the horizontal distance.
A person pulls a suitcase; the pulling force is shown at an angle of 30° to a horizontal dashed line.
A man holds a stretched bow and arrow, with the arrow pointing left.
A velocity-time graph with vertical axis velocity (m s⁻¹), horizontal axis time (s), a straight descending line from v to t, and O at the origin.
A roller coaster with a train on the track.

Two blocks shown at different heights above the ground; the lower block has an upward arrow labelled F and a downward arrow labelled w, and the height between the raised block and the ground is labelled h.
A waterfall, with water flowing over a wide rocky edge into a pool below.
A vertical diagram showing points A, B and C; a body at B between A and C; the distance from A to C is labelled h, and the distance from B to C is labelled x.
A coal-fired electricity generation plant showing Coal supply, Steam line, Turbine, Generator, Transmission lines, Condenser, Transformer and Water supply.
An old lantern.
A hydroelectric dam showing Transmission tower, Transformer, Water reservoir, Water intake, Bed rock, Tunnel, Generator, Turbine and Water discharge (canal).
A solar panel installed on a roof. Caption: Solar panels installed on the roof
Solar panels installed on a rooftop. Caption: Solar cells panels
A solar-powered car. Caption: Solar powered car which won the world solar challenge race in Darwin, Australia in 1993.
An Earth satellite in space. Caption: Earth satellites get solar energy through their solar panels.

Geothermal power plant diagram showing hot rocks underground, water entering through one hole and steam coming out through another to turn a turbine connected to a generator and transmission lines. Labels: Turbine, Generator, Transmission lines, Steam out, Water in, Hot rocks.
A geyser shooting a tall plume of water and steam into the air in a rocky landscape.
Windmills along a shoreline, with mountains in the background.
A wave-energy device with labels “Duck floats”, “Balance float”, and “Waves”.
A large, round biogas digester with a dark domed top and pale circular base, outdoors among trees.
Industrial chimneys emitting smoke and steam.
A person walking up stairs; the vertical height is labelled “height (h)”.
An inclined slope with a block on it and another block at the top. An arrow points up the slope; a dimension arrow along the slope is labelled 20 m, and a vertical dimension arrow is labelled 10 m.
A person pushing a lawn mower outdoors.
A box on an inclined plane labelled 10 m and 30°, with the vertical height labelled h.
A large coil spring surrounded by smaller springs and mechanical components on a technical-looking background.
A tennis ball against the strings of a tennis racket. Caption: Fig. 6.1
A graph with vertical axis F (N) and horizontal axis x (m), both with arrows. A straight line rises from O to A, then curves and levels off; “Elastic limit” is marked near A.
A helical spring suspended from a stand beside a vertical scale, with a pointer and a weight hanging from the spring.
Two spring scales; caption: “Spring scales”.
Mechanical clock balance wheel gears with the label “Balancing spring”.
Inside of a galvanometer, with the label “UPPER HAIRSPRING”; caption: “Inside of a Galvanometer”.
A container showing layers of liquid.
A measuring cylinder containing liquid and a solid at the bottom, with marks showing the liquid level.
Two pictures of a person carrying a bag, showing a larger area of contact in the right-hand picture than in the left-hand picture.
Two sports boot soles with studs and a red high-heeled shoe.
A person chopping vegetables on a cutting board. Caption: Fig. 6.6 Chopper
A finger pressing a thumb pin into a surface. Caption: Fig. 6.7 Thumb pin
A bulldozer with broad tracks on the ground.
A rectangular container holding liquid, with a submerged horizontal area marked A. A vertical double arrow marks depth h; downward arrows are labelled mg and P. Caption: Pressure in a liquid.
A container of water with three holes at different heights; streams of water flow out and curve down at different distances. Labels: “LOWEST PRESSURE”, “WATER”, “HIGHEST PRESSURE”.
A person squeezes a polythene bag containing water above a container while another person points toward the bag.
An upright tin can on a stand over a burner, and a hand pouring water onto a crumpled tin can.
A barometer consisting of a glass tube inverted in a dish of mercury. Labels: Glass tube, Vacuum, Scale, Air pressure, A, B. Caption: Fig. 6.9 Barometer
An air pressure gauge with a dial and hose. Caption: Air pressure guage which is used to measure the pressure in motor car tyres.
A Fortin’s barometer. Labels: Scale, Brass Tube, Barometer tube, Mercury, Mercury Reservoir. Caption: A Fortin's Barometer is used in laboratories to measure the atmospheric pressure.

A U-shaped tube containing mercury, with its two mercury levels shown equal by a dotted horizontal line. The left arm opens horizontally, with an arrow pointing into it; the right arm opens vertically, with a downward arrow above it. Caption: “Fig. 6.10 manometer”.

A U-shaped tube with a gas cylinder connected to the left arm and the right arm open. The mercury level is lower in the left arm than in the right arm; dashed horizontal lines mark the two levels, with a vertical double-headed arrow labelled “h” between them. “Air pressure” is labelled beside a downward arrow above the right arm. Caption: “Fig. 6.11”.

A U-shaped tube with the left arm open and a gas cylinder connected to the right arm. The mercury level is lower in the left arm than in the right arm; dashed horizontal lines mark the two levels, with a vertical double-headed arrow labelled “h” between them. A downward arrow is above the left arm, and “Gas cylinder” is labelled beside the cylinder. Caption: “Fig. 6.12”.
A flask containing water with a piston and side tubes. Labels: Piston, Side tubes, Flask, Water.
